# Diana Barry

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v1 c8 P37](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0037)</sub>
- **Origin:** Orchard Slope  <sub>[v1 c8 P37](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0037)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Di  <sub>[v1 c18 P25](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0025), [v3 c1 P17](../source/v03-c01.md#nw-v03-c01-p0017)</sub>

## Appearance

She is a very pretty girl with black eyes and hair, rosy cheeks, and dimples. She inherits her merry expression from her father, and possesses a fine snap and color in her look.

_Sources: [v1 c8 P40](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0040), [v1 c12 P21](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0021), [v1 c30 P43](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0043), [v3 c2 P4](../source/v03-c02.md#nw-v03-c02-p0004)_

## Personality

She is described as good, smart, and nice. She is fond of reading books, sometimes to the point of straining her eyes.

_Sources: [v1 c8 P37](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0037), [v1 c8 P40](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0040), [v1 c12 P21](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0021), [v1 c12 P22](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0022)_

## Traits

- good  <sub>[v1 c8 P40](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0040)</sub>

## Abilities

- making red tissue paper bookmarkers  <sub>[v1 c17 P29](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0029)</sub>

## History

Diana Barry grows up at Orchard Slope as a close playmate and bosom friend of Anne Shirley, taking a solemn oath of eternal friendship with her in the garden. Although briefly forbidden by her strict mother from playing with Anne after an incident, their bond is restored after Anne saves Diana's sister Minnie May from croup. When the Avonlea Village Improvement Society is established, Diana serves as its treasurer. As she grows up, she enters a romance with Fred Wright, whom she eventually marries in a evening ceremony before moving away to their new home.

_Sources: [v1 c8 P37](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0037), [v1 c12 P35](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0035), [v1 c17 P29](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0029), [v1 c18 P21](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0021), [v1 c18 P25](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0025), [v2 c6 P8](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0008), [v2 c29 P11](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0011), [v2 c29 P15](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0015), [v3 c29 P13](../source/v03-c29.md#nw-v03-c29-p0013)_

## Quotes

> Dear Anne, ran the former, “Mother says I’m not to play with you or talk to you even in school. It isn’t my fault and don’t be cross at me, because I love you as much as ever. I miss you awfully to tell all my secrets to and I don’t like Gertie Pye one bit. I made you one of the new bookmarkers out of red tissue paper. They are awfully fashionable now and only three girls in school know how to make them. When you look at it remember  <sub>[v1 c17 P29](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0029)</sub>

> Oh, Anne, do come quick,” implored Diana nervously. “Minnie May is awful sick—she’s got croup. Young Mary Joe says—and Father and Mother are away to town and there’s nobody to go for the doctor. Minnie May is awful bad and Young Mary Joe doesn’t know what to do—and oh, Anne, I’m so scared!  <sub>[v1 c18 P21](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0021)</sub>
